sourceSnapshots.openstax:introductory-statistics#2-key-t: histogram: a graphical representation in x-y form of the distribution of data in a data set; x represents the data and y represents the frequency, or relative frequency. The graph consists of contiguous rectangles. frequency: the number of times a value of the data occurs. relative frequency: the ratio of the number of times a value of the data occurs in the set of all outcomes to the number of all outcomes. box plot: a graph that gives a quick picture of the middle 50% of the data. outlier: an observation that does not fit the rest of the data.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:introductory-statistics#8-key-t: confidence interval (CI): an interval estimate for an unknown population parameter. This depends on: the desired confidence level, information that is known about the distribution (for example, known standard deviation), the sample and its size. confidence level (CL): the percent expression for the probability that the confidence interval contains the true population parameter; for example, if the CL = 90%, then in 90 out of 100 samples the interval estimate will enclose the true population parameter. error bound for a population mean (EBM): the margin of error; depends on the confidence level, sample size, and known or estimated population standard deviation. point estimate: a single number computed from a sample and used to estimate a population parameter.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:introductory-statistics#6-1: The standardized normal distribution is a type of normal distribution, with a mean of 0 and standard deviation of 1. It represents a distribution of standardized scores, called z-scores, as opposed to raw scores. A z-score indicates the number of standard deviation a score falls above or below the mean. Z-scores allow for comparison of scores, occurring in different data sets, with different means and standard deviations. A z-score is calculated as z=(x-μ)/σ. The standard normal distribution has a mean of 0 and standard deviation of 1.
sourceSnapshots.openstax:introductory-statistics#12-3: The process of fitting the best-fit line is called linear regression. The idea behind finding the best-fit line is based on the assumption that the data are scattered about a straight line. The criteria for the best fit line is that the sum of the squared errors is minimized. The absolute value of a residual measures the vertical distance between the actual value of y and the estimated value of y. The slope of the best-fit line tells us how the dependent variable changes for every one unit increase in the independent variable, on average. You should not use the line to predict values outside the domain of the x-values in the sample data.

definition.text: A confidence interval is an interval estimate for an unknown population parameter.

anchor.quote: an interval estimate for an unknown population parameter

facts.text: A 90% confidence level describes a repeated-sampling procedure: across many samples, about 90 out of 100 intervals constructed by that method will enclose the true population parameter.

anchor.quote: if the CL = 90%, then in 90 out of 100 samples the interval estimate will enclose the true population parameter

facts.text: The margin of error depends on the confidence level, the sample size, and the population standard deviation.

anchor.quote: depends on the confidence level, sample size, and known or estimated population standard deviation

facts.text: A point estimate is a single number computed from a sample and used to estimate a population parameter.

anchor.quote: a single number computed from a sample and used to estimate a population parameter

facts.text: A confidence interval depends on the desired confidence level, what is known about the distribution, and the sample size.

anchor.quote: the desired confidence level, information that is known about the distribution

misconceptions.text: Students read a 95% confidence interval as a 95% probability that the parameter lies inside the one interval they computed.
misconceptions.corrective: The confidence level describes the procedure across repeated samples — at CL = 90%, in 90 out of 100 samples the interval estimate encloses the parameter — rather than a probability attached to a single interval already calculated.

examples.text: A poll reporting 46% support with a three-point margin of error at 95% confidence describes how often intervals built this way capture the true share, not the odds for this one poll.

mcBank.stem: A 95% confidence level tells you that
options: intervals built this way capture the parameter 95% of the time
this particular interval has a 95% chance of being right now
95% of the sampled observations fall inside the interval
the sample mean equals the population mean in 95% of cases

definition.text: A histogram is a graphical representation in x-y form of the distribution of data in a data set.

anchor.quote: a graphical representation in x-y form of the distribution of data in a data set

facts.text: In a histogram the x-axis carries the data and the y-axis the frequency, and the graph consists of contiguous rectangles.

anchor.quote: x represents the data and y represents the frequency, or relative frequency. The graph consists of contiguous rectangles

facts.text: A box plot gives a quick picture of the middle 50% of the data.

anchor.quote: a graph that gives a quick picture of the middle 50% of the data

facts.text: An outlier is an observation that does not fit the rest of the data.

anchor.quote: an observation that does not fit the rest of the data

facts.text: Relative frequency is the ratio of the times a value occurs to the number of all outcomes.

anchor.quote: the ratio of the number of times a value of the data occurs in the set of all outcomes to the number of all outcomes

misconceptions.text: Students read a histogram like a bar chart of separate categories and treat the spacing between bars as meaningless decoration.
misconceptions.corrective: A histogram's rectangles are contiguous because the horizontal axis carries continuous data, so a visible gap reports an interval with zero frequency rather than a break between unrelated categories.

examples.text: A histogram of commute times shows the shape of the whole distribution, while a box plot of the same data shows where the middle half sits and flags observations that do not fit the rest.

mcBank.stem: Histogram rectangles are drawn contiguously because
options: the horizontal axis represents a continuous data range
every interval is required to contain at least one observation
the vertical axis always shows relative frequency
adjacent categories are unrelated to one another

kernels.attribution: OpenStax, Introductory Statistics, Ch. 2 Key Terms

definition.text: The standard normal distribution is a normal distribution with a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one.

anchor.quote: The standard normal distribution has a mean of 0 and standard deviation of 1

facts.text: A z-score states how many standard deviations a score falls above or below the mean.

anchor.quote: A z-score indicates the number of standard deviation a score falls above or below the mean
A z-score is calculated as z=(x-μ)/σ

facts.text: Z-scores allow comparisons between data sets with different means and standard deviations.

anchor.quote: Z-scores allow for comparison of scores, occurring in different data sets, with different means and standard deviations

facts.text: Standardized values are z-scores rather than the original raw scores.

anchor.quote: It represents a distribution of standardized scores, called z-scores, as opposed to raw scores

misconceptions.text: Students treat a positive z-score as a probability rather than a signed distance from the mean.
misconceptions.corrective: Read the sign as direction and the magnitude as the number of standard deviations from the mean.

examples.text: A score with z=-1.5 lies 1.5 standard deviations below its distribution's mean.

mcBank.stem: A z-score of -2 means the observation is
options: two standard deviations below the mean
two raw units below the mean

definition.text: Linear regression is the process of fitting a best-fit line to paired data.

anchor.quote: The process of fitting the best-fit line is called linear regression

facts.text: The least-squares best-fit line minimizes the sum of squared errors.

anchor.quote: The criteria for the best fit line is that the sum of the squared errors is minimized

facts.text: The absolute residual is the vertical distance between the observed response and its fitted value.

anchor.quote: The absolute value of a residual measures the vertical distance between the actual value of y and the estimated value of y

facts.text: The slope gives the average change in the dependent variable for a one-unit increase in the independent variable.

anchor.quote: The slope of the best-fit line tells us how the dependent variable changes for every one unit increase in the independent variable, on average

facts.text: A fitted line should not be used to predict beyond the observed domain of the explanatory variable.

anchor.quote: You should not use the line to predict values outside the domain of the x-values in the sample data

misconceptions.text: Students interpret a fitted line as proof that the explanatory variable causes the response.
misconceptions.corrective: Regression describes a fitted association; causal interpretation requires a design that supports causation.

examples.text: After fitting a line to paired observations, inspect residuals and keep predictions inside the observed x-range.

mcBank.stem: Why should a residual plot be checked after fitting a regression line?
options: It shows how observed responses differ from fitted values
It proves the explanatory variable caused the response
It guarantees predictions outside the observed x-range
It replaces the need to inspect the original paired data
